ai.description: *Hemidactylus acanthopholis* reaches 55 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal spots and possesses distinctive, enlarged, sharply keeled, spine-like tubercles arranged in longitudinal rows.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus acanthopholis* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of a distinct, longitudinal row of enlarged, sharply pointed, spine-like tubercles along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus acanthopholis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, typically inhabiting moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus acanthopholis* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates on rocky surfaces or tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus acanthopholis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus acanthopholis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, specifically inhabiting elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
